title: What Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0 Is

title: Real Research Today: Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0
definition: Today's documented research behind Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0.
description:
The road to Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0 is already being paved. The Delayed-Tolerant Networking standards (IETF, NASA) underpin the interplanetary internet. Meta's EMG wristband and Neuralink's implants advance neural input devices.

The DARPA N3 program develops noninvasive brain-computer interfaces for communication. Together these programs form the sat buses foundation that Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0 will build on — the constellation logistics results, the debris mitigation methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as constellation logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Satellite Mega-Constellations 2.0 — next-gen tens of thousands of broadband satellites.

Phase 1 — Prove (sat buses): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (constellation logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (debris mitigation): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (ground terminals): constellation hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and orbit-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
